item.title: A Decade After Brexit: Navigating the New Age of Barriers in European Finance Issues
item.content:encoded:
Steven Ongena, University of Zurich

Nam Vu, Miami University

Kiet Tuan Duong, University of York

Luu Duc Toan Huynh, Queen Mary University of London

A decade after the Brexit referendum, the financial landscape has transformed dramatically with increased protectionism, geopolitical tensions, and global economic fragmentation. This special issue examines how the UK's departure from the European Union reflects broader trends toward economic nationalism and regional separation, and how financial institutions are adapting to this new environment of barriers and reduced international integration.

The special issue seeks contributions exploring the long-term financial effects of Brexit on markets and services, the impact of recent trade policies on international finance, and how overlapping trade barriers affect equity and debt markets. Additional focus areas include regional financial inequalities, industrial policy effectiveness, institutional responses to fragmentation, syndicated lending disparities, regulatory approaches, fintech diffusion challenges, household financial behavior, and corporate governance changes among British and European firms.

Appel publié par The European Journal of Finance. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • The long-term effects of Brexit on UK and EU financial markets and financial services a decade after withdrawal
  • The macro-financial implications of Trump 2.0 trade policies for the UK, particularly in the context of renewed tariff regimes affecting British exports and imports and their global financial spillovers
  • The broader impact of overlapping trade barriers—including economic sanctions and retaliatory trade measures—on equity and debt markets
  • Regional disparities and financial inequalities in credit access and banking systems are exacerbated by trade and financial fragmentation
  • The resurgence of industrial policy and its effectiveness in promoting financial resilience under conditions of reduced international integration
  • Institutional responses and the capacity of international and regional organisations to mediate and stabilise an increasingly fragmented economic and financial order
  • Disparities in syndicated lending between UK and European lenders and borrowers, with particular attention to sustainable finance
  • The role of regulation and policymaking in reconnecting, or further decoupling, British and European financial systems
  • Barriers to financial technology diffusion following Brexit and the practical implementation of Brexit since 2020
  • Financial behaviour and household finance (e.g., financial flows, savings, investment decisions, overreactions, and reversal effects) ten years after Brexit
  • Changes in corporate governance among British and/or European firms, particularly shifts in board composition and the associated financial consequences

Timeline

  • March 1, 2026: Submissions open
  • September 30, 2026: Manuscript deadline

item.title: Generative AI and LLM in financial modelling and applications
item.content:encoded:
Steve Yang, Stevens Institute of Technology

Jing Chen, Cardiff University

Aparna Gupta, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute

Zachary Feinstein, Stevens Institute of Technology

William Knottenbelt, Imperial College

This special issue examines how Generative AI and Large Language Models are transforming financial modelling and applications. It welcomes research that explores AI's impact on traditional finance areas including asset pricing, financial intermediation, markets and investment, behavioral finance, banking, accounting, and insurance. The editors are particularly interested in work addressing ethical implications, financial inclusion benefits, and regulatory changes driven by these technologies.

The rapid adoption of tools like ChatGPT has sparked renewed interest in AI applications within finance. While Generative AI shows promise for enhancing data generation, analysis, decision-making, and risk management, research on its modelling and applications remains nascent. Simultaneously, significant challenges have emerged around data privacy, regulatory frameworks, innovation disruption, and the need to maintain human-centered approaches in financial systems.

Appel publié par The European Journal of Finance. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Asset pricing models using Generative AI and LLMs
  • Financial intermediation applications of AI technologies
  • Generative AI applications in financial markets and investment analysis
  • Behavioral finance research incorporating LLM insights
  • Banking sector applications of Generative AI
  • Accounting and auditing with LLM technologies
  • Insurance industry applications of AI and LLMs
  • Ethical implications of Generative AI in finance
  • Financial inclusion benefits through AI/LLM innovations
  • Regulatory and policy changes driven by Generative AI
  • Data generation and analysis using LLMs in finance
  • Risk management with Generative AI and LLMs
  • Natural language processing applications in finance
  • Information processing improvements through FinBERT and similar models
  • Data privacy concerns in AI-driven finance
  • Regulatory challenges of Generative AI in financial systems

Timeline

  • September 15, 2026: Manuscript deadline
